newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's son-in-law to head Aeroflot.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's son-in-law to head Aeroflot.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's son-in-law was named acting head of Aeroflot, Russia's state airline, on Wednesday. He had been deputy head before Yeltsin appointed the company's previous chief to his Kremlin staff.

Valery Okulov, who is married to Yeltsin's elder daughter Yelena, was named by Aeroflot's board of directors. Outgoing chief executive Yevgeny Shaposhnikov, a former Soviet defence minister, became the president's aerospace adviser on Tuesday.

Okulov's appointment needs the approval of shareholders to become permanent, Aeroflot-Russian International Airlines said in a statement. Shareholders should meet in May or June. The state owns 51 percent. Its 14,000 employees hold the rest.

Okulov, 45, flew as a navigator on Aeroflot airliners for 20 years before entering the top management in June 1996. He and Yelena have a teenage daughter and a son, also known as Boris Yeltsin, who entered to a private school in England last year.
There was no indication that President Yeltsin, 66, played any part in Okulov's elevation. Many Russian media did not mention his relationship in reports of the appointment.
In Soviet times, it was common practice for family members of senior leaders to occupy positions of authority.

Yeltsin has often condemned the corruption of the communist regime, exemplified by the likes of Yuri Churbanov. Named deputy interior minister by his father-in-law Leonid Brezhnev, Churbanov was eventually jailed for bribery in 1988.

Aeroflot, shorn of much of its fleet and businesses by the break-up of the Soviet Union and the creation of hundreds of so-called "babyflots", has maintained the leading position on international routes from Russia, with 70 percent of traffic.

It has striven to modernise its fleet though, like other former Soviet airlines, it has been criticised over safety standards. One of its Airbus A310s crashed in Siberia in 1994 after the pilot let his teenage son take the controls.
